name: Labeled Sample Compression of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, always reconstruct the sole concept from the empty key. For $n\ge2$, fix a cyclic successor map. If a sample has a positive point, retain its labeled positive point and reconstruct that singleton. For a nonempty all-negative sample on a proper subset $A$ of the domain, retain a negative point of $A$ whose successor lies outside $A$, and reconstruct the successor singleton. Such a point exists because the cycle is not contained in $A$. Reconstruct any fixed singleton at the empty key, which handles the empty sample. All reconstructions are consistent. Two distinct full concepts rule out width zero.
